metadata.title: Dedicated Access Workstation (DAW) Linux SSPP
metadata.remarks: Operating system–specific System Security and Privacy Plan defining how Linux endpoints implement the Dedicated Access Workstation (DAW) trust tier.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional security and privacy baseline profile.

system-characteristics.system-description: A Linux Dedicated Access Workstation configured as a single-purpose, maximal-assurance execution environment for privileged administration and Level 4 data workflows.

props.name: inherits-from-sspp
props.remarks: This Linux SSPP inherits all DAW requirements, including all COBO L2 and COBO L1 inherited constraints.

props.name: supported-distributions
props.remarks: Only institution-approved, vendor-supported LTS Linux distributions are permitted for DAW use.

props.name: ownership-model
props.remarks: DAW Linux endpoint is owned by the institution.

props.name: management-model
props.remarks: DAW Linux endpoint is centrally enrolled, governed, and monitored using institutional management tooling.

props.name: execution-model
props.remarks: General productivity workloads (email, browsing, collaboration, office suites, development toolchains) are prohibited.

props.name: cryptographic-identity
props.remarks: Linux DAW identity must use TPM-backed non-exportable private keys, PKI-issued device certificates, and hardware-backed attestation.

props.name: cryptographic-compliance
props.remarks: Linux cryptographic subsystems must use FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules.

props.name: secure-boot-and-measurement
props.remarks: UEFI Secure Boot, measured boot, and attestation integration must be enabled and enforced.

props.name: full-disk-encryption
props.remarks: Full disk encryption must be enabled with keys protected by TPM-backed mechanisms.

props.name: baseline-hardening
props.remarks: Linux DAW configuration applies CIS Linux Benchmark Level 2 with additional DAW-specific hardening overlays.

props.name: mandatory-access-controls
props.remarks: Mandatory access controls must be enforcing and protected against runtime disablement.

props.name: kernel-and-execution-hardening
props.remarks: Kernel lockdown, module signing, read-only kernel parameters, and restricted execution paths must be enforced.

props.name: malware-and-threat-protection
props.remarks: Institution-approved endpoint threat detection, integrity monitoring, and containment tooling must be enabled.

props.name: network-access-model
props.remarks: DAW Linux endpoints may communicate only with approved administrative brokers, management services, and control planes.

props.name: eligible-data-classifications
props.remarks: DAW Linux endpoints are required for workflows involving Level 4 data.

props.name: non-equivalence-statement
props.remarks: DAW endpoint status does not confer automatic entitlement to Level 4 data; all access remains governed by Secure Data policies.

props.name: privileged-workloads-only
props.remarks: DAW Linux endpoints are limited to privileged administration, security operations, and high-risk institutional workflows.

props.name: lifecycle-governance
props.remarks: Enrollment, suspension, recovery, and retirement of DAW Linux endpoints require elevated approval and enhanced auditability.

system-implementation.remarks: This SSPP defines how Linux implements the DAW trust tier through maximal isolation, strict hardware-backed identity, enforced boot integrity, hardened kernel controls, and continuous posture assurance.

control-implementation.remarks: Linux DAW baselines, bootloader configuration, TPM integration, CIS Level 2 hardening with DAW overlays, kernel lockdown, and endpoint protection tooling implement this SSPP and are maintained as strictly controlled, versioned artifacts.
